classification.difficultyReason: Identify two pairs of similar triangles and combine their corresponding-side ratios to prove a product identity.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram and $P$ is any point on $BC$ produced. Prove that: $AR^2=RQ\times RP$.

spec.description: Unfilled parallelogram ABCD with BC extended through C to P. AP crosses BD at R and CD at Q. Ordinary source blue linework is reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD; AD is parallel to BP. A, R, Q and P occur in that order on AP. B, R and D are collinear; D, Q and C are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied geometry and labels are visible; no proof annotations or answers are shown.

answer.worked:
Since $AD\parallel BP$, $\angle RAD=\angle RPB$ (alternate angles). Also, $\angle ARD=\angle PRB$ (vertically opposite angles). Hence $\triangle ARD\sim\triangle PRB$ (AAA), so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AR}{RP}&=\frac{RD}{RB}.\end{align*}$$
Since $AB\parallel DQ$, $\angle RBA=\angle RDQ$ (alternate angles). Also, $\angle BRA=\angle DRQ$ (vertically opposite angles). Hence $\triangle BRA\sim\triangle DRQ$ (AAA), so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{RD}{RB}&=\frac{RQ}{AR}.\end{align*}$$
Combining these ratios,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AR}{RP}&=\frac{RQ}{AR}\\AR^2&=RQ\times RP.\end{align*}$$
